top.title: Start a handoff command's deadline when it takes its turn at the source

items.author: jeejeelee
items.summary: Fixes a FlashInfer Cake PDL race condition in gated_residual_rmsnorm by switching to the CuTe DSL backend, correcting corrupted hidden states causing garbage DSpark output at small row counts.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Run Muse Spark's `gated_residual_rmsnorm` on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL backend instead of the default Cake backend. The Cake programs for 128 rows or fewer read `branch` before `griddepcontrol.wait` (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9343). This corrupts the hidden states that DSpark reads, so DSpark output is garbage at DP + EP with TP=1. No open PR addresses this.

- Fixes DSpark at DEP8: AIME25 0% → 98.9%, GSM8K 23.1% → 94.8%, sdAL back to 3.7–3.9.
- No end-to-end perf change at TEP4.

items.title: [Fix] attention: Return zeros instead of NaN from merge_state_v2 when both states are empty
items.author: TanishGudise
items.summary: The Triton path is covered by #48796; this fixes the CUDA kernel. combines two partial attention states using their log-sum-exp values.
items.body:
## Motivation

The Triton path is covered by #48796; this fixes the CUDA kernel.

`merge_state_v2` (`kernels/aot/csrc/attention/merge_attn_states.cu`) combines two partial attention states using their log-sum-exp values. When a token is empty on both sides (both LSEs `-inf`, or `+inf`, which the kernel maps to `-inf`), `max_lse` is `-inf`, `-inf - (-inf)` makes both scales NaN, and the kernel writes NaN to the output and LSE. On sglang-kernel 0.4.10 (NVIDIA L4), a both-empty token gives NaN in every output element.

items.body:

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix M-RoPE position preparation when PCP is enabled- #66516
items.author: baolongsun
items.summary: Fixes incorrect M-RoPE 3D position computation under Prefill Context Parallelism by adding a PCP-aware path that correctly maps rank-local request fragments to their global positions.
items.body:
Added a new method to prepare M-RoPE positions for a PCP-local batch, handling both prefill and regular requests.



### Overview
This PR fixes M-RoPE position preparation under PCP for multimodal models.
PCP splits one request into rank-local fragments, but the original RopeState.prepare_positions() assumed a 1:1 mapping between local rows and global requests. For M-RoPE models, this produced incorrect 3D positions, especially for image inputs. This PR adds a PCP-aware path that reconstructs the correct 3D positions for each local fragment.
### Claims
- Fixes incorrect M-RoPE position

items.title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Opt-in whole-row regions for GQA caches under block-outermost layouts
items.author: TanishGudise
items.summary: With a block-outermost KV cache layout, every layer's page of a block sits in one contiguous row, but NixlConnector still registers one region per layer for full-attention (GQA) caches. A layer's consecutive blocks are then a whole row apart, so NIXL cannot me…
items.body:
## Overview

With a block-outermost KV cache layout (`VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`), every layer's page of a block sits in one contiguous row, but NixlConnector still registers one region per layer for full-attention (GQA) caches. A layer's consecutive blocks are then a whole row apart, so NIXL cannot merge them, and an 8k-token Llama-3.1-8B transfer is always 16,384 descriptors (32 layers x 512 blocks), however the blocks are laid out. items.author: he-yufeng
items.summary: The sending and receiving threads wait indefinitely in and have no shutdown handshake. After the five-second deadline it logs a warning and closes the store anyway.

## Bug Report

`MooncakeStoreWorker.close()` can release the native store while one of its transfer threads is still executing a store operation.

After the five-second deadline it logs a warning and closes the store anyway. If the blocked native operation then resumes, the live thread continues using the closed handle. Idle threads also remain alive after close.

## What this changes

This PR moves the NPU weight-migration and TP-reuse changes from #48835 onto current main. It supports `PP=1` with `TP=EP=WORLD`.

items.body:
## Motivation

In GDN/full-attention hybrid models, cached KV can extend beyond the reusable GDN state. Replaying tokens to restore GDN state then recomputes full-attention K/V that is already cached.

This PR reuses that KV, skipping K/V projections, K normalization/RoPE, and KV writes. All other replay computation remains unchanged.

## Modifications

- Add opt-in `SGLANG_ENABLE_GDN_KV_REUSE=1` (default off).
- Borrow and pin cached KV per request; compute and write K/V only for ordinary chunks. Support multiple requests, mixed reusable/ordinary batches, and overlap scheduling.
- Fix FP32 GD

## Motivation

On a multimodal model, a text-only chat completion feeds the model two BOS tokens when the tokenizer adds BOS (`add_bos_token`) and the chat template also writes it.

How it happens:
- `_can_reuse_text_only_prompt_ids` refuses the rendered ids whenever the tokenizer adds specials.

items.author: aijanai
items.summary: Prevents TP ranks from silently diverging on sampled tokens by adding collective sampler-backend agreement and startup config consistency checks at Sampler construction time.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #66912.

Every TP rank samples on the all-gathered logits and feeds **its own** sampled tokens into the next step; only TP rank 0's tokens reach the user, and nothing compares the ranks. ### Motivation

For hybrid linear-attention models (GDN, KDA, Mamba), SGLang splits the cache memory at startup into a KV pool and a state pool, by `--mamba-full-memory-ratio` (or a pinned `--max-mamba-cache-size`). ## Overview

Rust Chat Completions silently discarded the top-level `thinking` object, so a request such as `{"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}` still rendered the default thinking prompt. Normalize the supported controls through the existing reasoning path and reject unsupported inputs.

## Claims

- Honor explicit mode and effort: `thinking.type` overrides template toggle aliases, and `thinking.effort` overrides `reasoning_effort`. Omitted, null and empty objects preserve existing behavior.
- Support `keep="all"` for the native Kimi renderer: prior reasoning is retained when thinking is enab

Scheduler CPU per step scales with running requests × KV cache groups, because `allocate_slots` calls each single-type manager's `remove_skipped_blocks`, `get_num_blocks_to_allocate`, `allocate_new_blocks` and `cache_blocks` for every request on every step, even though most steps cross no block boundary in most groups. items.title: [Bug]: Gemma 4: a LoRA on k_proj is not applied to the value on attention_k_eq_v layers (silent mismatch with Transformers)
items.author: yizhao95
items.summary: Also reproduced on vLLM 0.33.0 (below). On the 31B these are the full-attention layers 5, 11,..., 59. [Discussion: I believe this issue has already been fixed by #61267.]
items.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.19.1, transformers 5.13.1, peft 0.21.2, torch 2.10.0+cu128, 1x RTX 5090 (vLLM in bfloat16; the Transformers side on CPU in float32). Also reproduced on vLLM 0.33.0 (below).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Some Gemma 4 layers have `attention_k_eq_v: true`. On the 31B these are the full-attention layers 5, 11, ..., 59. Those layers have no `v_proj`. In Transformers, the value is computed from the `k_proj` output (before `k_norm` and RoPE, followed by the weightless `v_norm`). A PEFT LoRA on `k_proj` therefore changes **both** the key and the value on those layers.
discussion: I believe this issue has already been fixed by #61267. Please feel free to reopen it if you encounter any further issues.

## Motivation

The processor's DeepSeek renderer (`attach_deepseek_tokenizer`) carries its own HF `tokenizers` instance built from `tokenizer.json`, and `ChatFormatter::encode` returns `encode_request`'s ids before the router's tokenizer is consulted. For DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, `--tokenizer-backend fast` therefore has no effect: every request re-encodes its whole prompt with HF.

On a DeepSeek-V4.1 PD deployment with ~100–200K-token agentic prompts, the router spent ~0.55 core-seconds per request, and the time from the router receiving a request to the engine logging it grew by ~5.5 ms per 1K promp

items.title: [Model][GLM-5.3] Load ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoints into BF16 attention and vision
items.author: Kh4L
items.summary: This PR lets vLLM load as published. It is a ModelOpt checkpoint. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

This PR lets vLLM load [`nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local) as published. It is a ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION` checkpoint.

GLM-5.3-Flash builds its attention (KDA, MLA, the MTP layer's MLA and indexer) and its vision tower in BF16, but this checkpoint quantizes those modules (MXFP8, FP8_PB_WO, W4A16_NVFP4). The PR dequantizes them to BF16 as they stream in, and lets the MTP draft resolve its layer's quantization.

Builds on #64739, which finds the checkpoint's `tensors/` shard, and on the CSF scale support from #64312 (merged).

## Motivation

Closes #49133.

Under Breakable Prefill CUDA Graph (BCG), short prefills and cached-prefix extends whose token count `M` is not an exact capture bucket are padded up to the next bucket (`13/14 -> 16`, `17/18 -> 20`, `21..23 -> 24`, `25..27 -> 28`, `29..31 -> 32`, `84 -> 96`, etc.). items.title: [Core][Perf] Exact-end Mamba checkpoints and GreedyDual-Size eviction for hybrid prefix caching
items.author: ischencheng
items.summary: Two prefix-caching options for hybrid models in Mamba mode, from the FlashState paper (https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.flashstate). Both are off by default. [Discussion: Documentation preview: https://vllm--66881.org.readthedocs.build/en/66881/]
items.body:
## Overview

Two prefix-caching options for hybrid models in Mamba `align` mode, from the FlashState paper (https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.flashstate). RFC #66844, part of #26201. Both are off by default.

- `--mamba-frontier-checkpoint`: when a request finishes, its Mamba state and its last partial KV page are cached at its exact length, so the next turn of an agent session resumes there instead of at the last block boundary of its prompt.
- `--prefix-cache-eviction gds --prefill-cost-coefficients D E`: a state and the KV pages only it needs are kept or evicted together, ordered by GreedyD

items.title: [Fix] sgl-router: Render and tokenize off the async workers
items.author: Kangyan-Zhou
items.summary: Prevents synchronous render/tokenize work from blocking tokio async workers in sgl-router by using block_in_place, avoiding full router stalls under load.
items.body:
## Motivation

Chat-template rendering and tokenization are synchronous CPU work, and today they run inside an async handler's poll. When one render is slow (a long conversation, or a template that does a lot of work per message), the tokio worker running it is stuck in that poll. The other workers stay parked and nothing polls the I/O driver, so the whole router stops serving: no new connections are accepted, HTTP/2 PINGs go unanswered, and in-flight streams get no bytes until the render returns. Under load, a single multi-second render can make clients and proxies drop every open connection

### Motivation

Tensor parallelism across nodes linked by commodity Ethernet (25 GbE RoCE between workstations or DGX Spark-class boxes) pays one all-reduce per block per step. At decode batch sizes that all-reduce is latency-bound: we measured about 66 us for TP4 and 36-40 us for TP2 over 25 GbE at batch 1 (inside a CUDA graph), against 2-3 us on one PCIe node. That is the same order as reading a mixer's weights from HBM, so for some blocks it is cheaper to keep the block whole on every rank (replicate it) and skip its all-reduce than to shard it.

## Overview

`wo_b` reads row-major `[M, K/32]` MXFP8, and the conc-64 `wo_a` tile writes its output columns in groups of 32, so the quant can be written in the `wo_a` epilogue and the separate quant launch between `wo_a` and `wo_b` disappears. Tiles narrower than one MX block cannot quantize in the epilogue, so they keep `wo_b`'s own quant path. The choice depends on the token count, so it lives in an opaque custom op (`rocm_dsv41_mxfp8_o_proj`) rather than in the compiled graph. The aiter preshuffle path (`_wo_b_scale`) quantizes inside its own GEMM and is left untouched.

## Overview

`kpool_decode_update_and_maybe_write_cache_batched` launches the batched decode-update kernel without `num_warps`, so Triton's default of 4 gives 256 lanes for a 128-element block. This clamps `num_warps` to the block width, as `dflash2_conv_ops.py` already does for the same issue.

This PR tiles the fused RoPE + KV write on gfx1250 once T is at least 256. The existing kernel launches one 1-warp program per token per query head.

## Motivation

On gfx1250 that per-(token, head) launch sits around 0.6 TB/s for a prefill-sized T. gpt-oss-120b, TP1, T=16384: 586 us.

## Overview

Adds an opt-in encoder length bucketing mechanism that regroups a padded audio-encoder batch by true item length into discrete length rungs, so short clips stop paying for the padding of long clips. Qwen2-Audio is adapted as the first (mask-aware) model.

This **complements, not replaces**, the existing packed-varlen path (`MMEncoderAttention` + `cu_seqlens`): varlen packs items losslessly where the encoder function is unchanged by packing, while bucketing recovers the padding waste where packing does not apply. items.title: Restore GC when a direct-mode MegatronLLM shuts down
items.author: lmcafee-nvidia
items.summary: Fixes direct-mode MegatronLLM failing to re-enable Python GC and unfreeze the heap on shutdown, causing permanent object freezing and CUDA OOM leaks.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

With main's default `gc_mode="freeze_overlap"`, a dynamic engine freezes the Python heap
when its first batch drains and then disables automatic garbage collection, collecting
only right after each forward pass. Only `suspend()` and the coordinator loop's
`shutdown()` leave that mode.

items.body:
### Why

A checkpoint worker owns one GPU, but Ray's first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key includes the local device ordinal. With shared GPU visibility, workers using `cuda:0` and `cuda:3` can therefore join unintended devices or wait on different rendezvous keys. Masked workers, which all see `cuda:0`, hide this assumption.

### Change

Let the checkpoint engine own a device-bound NCCL group with a logical rendezvous key. Use that device for the barrier, buffer allocation, executor-thread broadcasts and group destruction. Delta transfers use the same path. Ordinar

## Summary

`_decode_step_prep_kernel`, the bookkeeping kernel of the batch-invariant Mamba decode, reads the slot's write cursor `num_buffered[slot]` in every thread of a program and has one thread store the advanced cursor at the end. The threads of a Triton program are not synchronized with each other, and the kernel launches with four warps. A warp that reaches the load after that store uses the advanced cursor and copies its elements of the token's x / dt / B / C rows into the next buffer row (row 0 after a crossing).

The row that the scan then reads keeps the values of one chunk earlier

## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

slime runs its own training loop and steps `opt_param_scheduler` once per successful optimizer update. It never advances `args.consumed_train_samples`, which Megatron's own loop maintains, so every checkpoint stores 0.

## Overview


After the engine output dispatcher terminates, the Rust API server becomes
unhealthy but continues listening and returning failed responses indefinitely.

Monitor permanent LLM health failures, stop the HTTP and gRPC servers, complete
resource cleanup, and return an error so process managers can restart the
frontend.

This aligns the Rust frontend with the Python server behavior: exit on engine
failure by default while honoring `VLLM_KEEP_ALIVE_ON_ENGINE_DEATH`.



## Claims

- Exit with a nonzero status when the LLM becomes permanently unhealthy.

Cache-aware admission examines only its configured head window, but every successful reorder rebuilt the entire FCFS waiting queue. Remove exactly that head before restoring the reordered requests so the cost no longer grows with the backlog.

items.title: [Perf][Attention] Cache Triton K/V cache views per tensor identity
items.author: huangsiyuan0422
items.summary: re-derives K/V cache views ( + optional FP8 ) on every attention call across,, and, even though these views depend only on the tensor's storage/shape/strides, which are fixed once the cache is allocated. This adds ~5-7 us of host overhead per attention layer p…
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #64572.

`TritonAttentionImpl` re-derives K/V cache views (`transpose(1, 2).split` + optional FP8 `view`) on every attention call across `forward`, `do_kv_cache_update`, and `do_rope_and_kv_cache_update`, even though these views depend only on the `kv_cache` tensor's storage/shape/strides, which are fixed once the cache is allocated.

This adds ~5-7 us of host overhead per attention layer per step, which is significant on the eager (non-torch.compile) path.

## Fix

Add `_get_kv_views` which derives and caches the K/V views (and FP8 retype) once per `kv_cache` tensor identity

## Problem

With `--cuda-graph-impl full_iteration`, `FullCudaGraphWrapper` captures the whole forward/backward, including `forward_step` / `get_batch`. The per-iteration sequence statistics therefore split into two halves that behave differently under replay:

- `_seqlen_stats_in_iteration` is a device tensor, so `update_seqlen_stats_from_cu_seqlens`'s `+=` is captured and replayed;
- `_seqlen_stats_active` is Python state, set only while capturing.

Once `consume_seqlen_stats_in_iteration` drains the capture iteration and clears the flag, every later replayed iteration reports `(None, None)`

# What does this PR do?

`prepare_trajectories` sets a pad token only for the Hugging Face and TikToken libraries. items.title: [#21912][perf] Avoid full priority-queue scans for bounded peeks
items.author: Hang-get
items.summary: Priority scheduling with KV-balanced attention-DP admission calls every admitting iteration. The existing implementation scans the entire waiting queue even though the admission window is normally 32 requests.
items.body:
## Description

Priority scheduling with KV-balanced attention-DP admission calls `PriorityWaitingQueue.peek_requests` every admitting iteration. The existing `heapq.nsmallest` implementation scans the entire waiting queue even though the admission window is normally 32 requests.

Use a best-first frontier over the existing min-heap for bounded peeks. It visits only the relevant heap branches, reducing the bounded path from O(n log k) to O(k log k) without mutating or copying the source heap. Requests for at least one quarter of the queue retain the existing `nsmallest` path.

Closes #21912.

items.title: fix(inference): reserve recurrent-state dummy slot when tp_ep > 1
items.author: lauradang
items.summary: A hybrid (Mamba) engine with TP > 1 and EP = 1 (e.g. TP=2, EP=1) can crash with. [Discussion: Auto-sync is disabled for draft pull requests in this repository.]
items.body:
## What

A hybrid (Mamba) engine with TP > 1 and EP = 1 (e.g. TP=2, EP=1) can crash with `No free recurrent-state slots for 1 expert-parallel dummy request(s)`.

The engine's work consensus runs over the `tp_ep` group (expert TP x EP), and between refreshes it reuses a cached result. After local work drains, the stale cache can still say "there is work", so the engine runs a dummy forward. That dummy forward needs a recurrent-state slot, but the dedicated dummy slot was only reserved for EP > 1. On a prefill engine whose slots are all held by pending KV handoffs, allocation fails.

**The fix.*

items.title: Fix dataloader checkpoint directory creation on every writing rank
items.author: jwills
items.summary: When external dataloader state is saved per data-parallel rank, only DP rank 0 currently creates the checkpoint's parent directory. A distributed barrier synchronizes ranks but does not guarantee directory visibility across node-local filesystem mounts.
items.body:
When external dataloader state is saved per data-parallel rank, only DP rank 0 currently creates the checkpoint's parent directory. A distributed barrier synchronizes ranks but does not guarantee directory visibility across node-local filesystem mounts. A nonzero writing rank can therefore reach `torch.save` without its parent directory and fail.

Call `ensure_directory_exists` on every rank that writes a state file. Rank-independent loaders retain their rank-0-only writes. Extend the explicit-process-groups regression test, which uses DP rank 3, to assert that the parent directory exists.

### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, `response_only_lm_head` (default `false`). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head. With the option on, the engine passes the packed rows that predict response tokens to the model as Transformers' `logits_to_keep`, so the eager and fused LM heads project only those rows. The values at response tokens are unchanged.

items.title: [ckpt, worker] feat: mori checkpoint engine sharded export (no trainer all-gather)
items.author: lixiufei-leo
items.summary: This is a follow-up to #8482 (the checkpoint engine) and builds on it; only the last commit is new. Each trainer rank sends only its own shards from the training engine's, in bf16 and using the contract in, so the trainer no longer all-gathers every parameter.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

This is a follow-up to #8482 (the `mori` checkpoint engine) and builds on it; only the last commit is new. It adds `export: shard`. items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

items.author: chaoworks
items.summary: inserts serialized runtime environment JSON inside literal single quotes. An environment value such as makes Bash reject the command before Ray starts; paired apostrophes can instead be silently removed from the value.
items.body:

items.body:
## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8433.

`SFTTrainer` built its train/val `StatefulDataLoader`s without a `generator`, so every iterator construction drew a `base_seed` from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores `torch.get_rng_state()`, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted run. This PR gives each dataloader its own seeded `torch.Generator`, so building iterators no longer touches the global CPU RNG and the restored state is the one training actually continues with.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Add M3.1-Flash multimodal input handling and public-checkpoint-layout full-weight export to the **VeOmni training / vLLM rollout** path. This enables the full-parameter M3.1-Flash integration without adding generic LoRA support.

The target checkpoint is **MiniMax-M3.1-Flash**. Its checkpoint config uses `model_type="minimax_m3_vl"` and architecture `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration`; existing `minimax_m3` module/class identifiers are retained for compatibility. They are architecture identifiers, not a claim that a different model version was validated.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Reserve vLLM engine ports on the IPv4/IPv6 wildcard listener scope while retaining the advertised NIC address. Reserving only the advertised interface can leave the wildcard address used by the engine available to another listener.

Reservations remain held during configuration and are released immediately before engine creation. Partial allocation, launch errors and cancellation release owned sockets; cleanup is idempotent.

With `--partial-rollout`, a sample aborted mid-generation goes back to the data buffer and is resumed later. `generate()` resumes it with a `max_new_tokens` budget reduced by `sample.response_length` and appends the new tokens after the existing response, so the request must be conditioned on that response.

For samples with images, the request is built as:

```python

payload["text"] = sample.prompt
```

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

`_wait_server_healthy()` calls `requests.get(.../health)` without a timeout. If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach `is_process_alive()`.

## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

## Approach

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.
